This page documents a [[id:699A8D45-B67E-4D3E-9206-24FA17C51ADA][story]] in [[id:2B39B97B-89F9-4320-8BAC-A603D805EBF3][Sprint 26]]. It captures the goal, current status, acceptance criteria, and the tasks that compose it.

* Goal

Each of diff, compute, telemetry, history, scheduler, ore, variability and workspace either renders the shell units generation produces or states, model by model, the reason it renders none, and every hand-written command that survives is recorded with its reason.

* Acceptance

- Every entity, junction and operation model in these components either renders a generated shell unit or states the reason it renders none in its own Physical space section.
- Every hand-written command in the component's orbit is compared with the generated units and either retired as superseded or recorded with its reason.
- Each component's shell suite passes and the codegen gates are green.

* Notes

- Survey on 2026-10-01 at =30251f222c=. The eight components and what each holds:

| Component | Models with no unit | Shell part |
|-----------+---------------------+------------|
| diff | 4 entities, all table-less records | none |
| compute | 3 entities, 2 operations | 8 units |
| telemetry | 3 operations | none |
| history | 1 operation | none |
| scheduler | 1 entity, 1 operation | none |
| ore | 1 operation, 1 entity | none |
| variability | 1 operation | 1 unit |
| workspace | 1 operation | 1 unit |

- The decisive fact is the shell part. A component with no part under
  =projects/ores.shell/= cannot host a generated unit at all, and five of the
  eight have none. =scheduler/job_definition= already states that reason in its own
  Physical space, which is the shape the rest of these tasks follow.
- =reporting= is out of scope. Its five unbound entities are the ones
  bright_faraday's task "Bind the standard profiles to the configuration entities
  that carry none" is binding now, and the shell facet follows from the profile.
- =http= is out of scope by decision.

* Decisions

- 2026-10-01. Where a model renders no shell unit and should not, the reason goes
  in the model's own =* Physical space= section, not on a task page. The repo
  already does this in =ores.scheduler.job_definition=, and a reason beside the
  thing it explains survives the reader who never opens the sprint.

* Out of scope

- =reporting=, whose profiles another environment is binding now.
- =http=, by decision.
- =trading= and =marketdata=, which are large enough to want their own story.

* Result

Merged in three batches, with every check green: PR #2477 for the scaffold and
diff, #2479 for compute and telemetry, and #2480 for history, scheduler, ore,
variability and workspace.

Nineteen models across the eight components now state, in their own Physical
space, why no shell command reaches them. That was the story's whole shape: five
of the eight have no part under =projects/ores.shell=, so generation could not
land a unit in them, and the work was to record that rather than to build the
parts.

Nothing was retired. None of the eight has a generated unit that duplicates one of
its hand-written commands, which is where this story differs from the first: the
first seven had eighteen superseded verbs, and these have none.

Two findings came out of it that are worth more than the records.

The first is a defect. Three compute models named =| ores.cpp.shell | false |=
in their Physical space tables. There is no =ores.cpp.shell= facet; the address is
=ores.cpp.shell-command=. The rows did nothing, and the shell units were withheld
only because =ores.cpp.protocol= happened to be off too. A validator over every
model's Physical space now reports no address that does not exist.

The second is a gap with a name. The scheduler's hand-written menu sends exactly
the requests the =job_definitions= unit and the =scheduling_operations= unit would
send, across five of its six verbs. It is the one place in the story where
generation would supersede a hand-written command the moment the component has a
shell part. Both models now say so, so the follow-up is written where the next
reader meets it.
